speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. Bilious vomiting in a newborn is a medical emergency; can you tell me exactly how many days old your baby is and when these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus. The history of bilious vomiting starting within six hours of birth in a term infant is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise, and while the family history of pyloric stenosis is noted, the age and nature of the symptoms strongly favor malrotation.
